answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to stake a deposit that is slashed when peers prove duplicate behavior, tying cost to every new account rather than to a whisper of intent. Verification should rest on a continuous thread of attested work history: agents earn reputation only through completed, checkable tasks over time, so a spawned swarm has no record to spend. Like shale formed under pressure, that history cannot be faked quickly; creating many credible identities costs more time and stake than the rewards they could extract, making mass forgery uneconomical.
